note: Home-networking silicon (HomePNA); acquired by Broadcom 1999 (~$316M). Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Consumer review site; merged with DealTime to form Shopping.com 2003, acquired by eBay 2005. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention

Online investment bank founded by Benchmark with Schwab, TD Waterhouse and Ameritrade; acquired by Goldman Sachs 2001. A fund-shaped NAME that is an operating company, so it stays in (COLLECTION.md §1, fund-shaped list entries)
Equinix (EQIX, Nasdaq); Benchmark in the 1998 first institutional round of the Al Avery/Jay Adelson carrier-neutral colocation company, years before the 2000 IPO
Open-source AWS-compatible private cloud (Marten Mickos); acquired by Hewlett-Packard 2014
Sports fan-data site on the 2010-2011 captures only, dark since, with no exit and no shutdown notice on the record — unknown rather than a guessed defunct
Real-time feed aggregator (Bret Taylor, Paul Buchheit); Benchmark led the 2008 Series A; acquired by Facebook 2009

Benchmark and Kleiner Perkins put ~$13M into Friendster in October 2003, the company's first institutional financing; the contemporary record calls it both an A and a B, so the label is low confidence. Wound down 2015; the Wikidata country (MY) is the last-known HQ after the 2009 sale to MOL Global and is left standing
Gaia Interactive's anime community and virtual world; on the 2010-2012 list, still operating at much reduced scale, no credible recent mark
Cloud game streaming (David Perry); acquired by Sony 2012 ($380M)

Sporting-goods retailer bought out of The Limited in 1995 by Freeman Spogli with Benchmark alongside; IPO 2001, acquired by Dick's Sporting Goods 2004. A buyout-scale, non-venture-round position: kept as a member on the firm's own listing, entry Growth by taxonomy, and RAISED as an open ruling — under the 2026-09-04 control-position addendum a transaction in which the firm's co-investor group takes control is out, and whether that reaches a minority co-investor in a 1995 retail LBO is Erik's boundary call, not a row fix
Call-centre software; IPO 1997, acquired by Alcatel 2000 ($1.5B), later Permira. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Chip-synthesis EDA; acquired by Cadence Design Systems 2003. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Employer reviews and salary data (Robert Hohman, Rich Barton — a Benchmark venture partner of the era); Benchmark led the 2008 first institutional round; acquired by Recruit Holdings 2018 ($1.2B)
Mobile device management, formerly Good Technology/Visto; Benchmark backed the early rounds from 2000-2001; acquired by BlackBerry 2015 ($425M). Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Social test-prep, later Learnist; acquired by Kaplan 2013

Benchmark led the $11M SERIES C in November 2010 — not the $20M March-2011 round, which was the Series D and DAG Ventures led it. Growth. IPO 2014, acquired by Just Eat Takeaway 2021 and sold on to Wonder 2025
Jeff Hawkins and Donna Dubinsky's Palm-OS handheld company; Benchmark in the 1998 first round; IPO 2000, merged into palmOne 2003
HipLogic (formerly Numobiq), mobile home-screen software; Lasky Form D seat 2009, in tenure; no exit and no shutdown on the record
The Hadoop company spun out of Yahoo; Benchmark led the $23M Series A in 2011; IPO 2014, merged with Cloudera 2019
Open-source infrastructure monitoring; acquired by SpringSource 2009 and so into VMware
Video-compression silicon; acquired by GlobespanVirata 2000 and so into Conexant. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention

Optical transport systems (founded 2000 as Zepton Networks); Benchmark in the early rounds from 2001-2003, on the firm's list from the 2003 capture; IPO 2007, acquired by Nokia 2025. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Pay-per-call advertising and the Ether marketplace; acquired by AT&T 2007

Burbn, Inc. — the row is the pre-rename entity the firm's own list carried. Benchmark led the $7M Series A in February 2011 at ~$25M (Matt Cohler on the board); acquired by Facebook April 2012 ($1B), so the standalone mark is retired
Smoothie retailer; Benchmark's growth position, IPO by SPAC 2006, acquired by Focus Brands 2018
JAMDAT Mobile, mobile games; Benchmark led the first round in 2000; IPO 2004, acquired by Electronic Arts 2006 ($680M)
Jasper Technologies, IoT connectivity management; acquired by Cisco 2016 ($1.4B) — the standalone mark is retired

Juniper Networks; Benchmark in the 1996-1997 early rounds of Pradeep Sindhu's router company, IPO 1998 — one of the firm's two founding-era wins with eBay. Acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise 2025, so the standalone mark is retired
Kana Communications, customer-service software; Benchmark in the 1997-1998 first rounds, IPO 1999; merged with Broadbase 2001 and later sold on

Klip, the mobile video app (Alain Rossmann); acquired by BlackBerry 2013. The deterministic layer put the HQ in the Netherlands, which does not fit the company — corrected to US with the dispute flagged rather than accepted or silently overwritten
Peer-assisted video delivery; acquired by VeriSign 2006, spun out 2008 and acquired by Kollective. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention

Linden Research, maker of Second Life; Benchmark in the early rounds from the 2000s. Bought by an investor group led by Randy Waterfield and Brad Oberwager in 2020 — a change of control, so the row reads acquired and the standalone mark is retired
Cloud contact centre and on-demand agent network; the platform business became Serenova (2017) and the agent business was sold on, so the standalone company no longer exists
Crowdsourced logo and identity design; acquired by Hewlett-Packard 2007

Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz's managed-hosting company; IPO 2001, sold the hosting business to EDS in 2002 and renamed itself OPSWARE, which HP acquired in 2007 ($1.6B). The base carries both rows — suspected duplicate of opsware, flagged for the identity-merge file rather than merged silently. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Search and social advertising management; IPO 2013, wound the business down and delisted in 2025 after selling its assets
Three-dimensional one-time-programmable memory; acquired by SanDisk 2006 (~$250M). Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention
Network behaviour analysis for DDoS and insider threat; acquired by Riverbed Technology 2009. Pre-2003 entry, Series A by convention

Metaweb Technologies, the Freebase knowledge graph (Danny Hillis, Robert Cook); Benchmark in the 2006 first institutional round and the 2008 $42M follow-on. ACQUIRED by Google in July 2010 — the deterministic layer read the later Freebase shutdown (2016) as the company being defunct, which is the wrong event: the corporate outcome was the acquisition, and the dispute is flagged rather than silently accepted
Mint.com personal finance; Bob Kagle's Form D seat 2009, in tenure; acquired by Intuit 2009 ($170M) and retired by Intuit in 2024
Minted, the crowdsourced design marketplace; on the 2012 capture, still operating, no credible recent primary mark
Adaptive-bitrate video delivery (American Fork, Utah); the assets were sold to EchoStar in 2010 after the business failed to scale
Mu Dynamics, network security and service assurance testing; acquired by Spirent Communications 2012

MySQL AB, the open-source database company; Benchmark and Index led the $19.5M round in 2003, after the company's first institutional financing, so the entry is Growth by taxonomy. Acquired by Sun Microsystems 2008 ($1B) and so into Oracle. The row sits on the HOME desk because the firm's own post-split 2010-2013 list carries it (decisions.md D4.1), although Benchmark Europe was also in the deal; last-known HQ Uppsala, Sweden
